body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending in the present application. Claim 1, 5, 6, and 17 is amended in this paper. No claims are canceled in this paper. No new claims are added in this paper.
In taking the foregoing actions, Applicant respectfully submits Applicant is not

necessarily conceding in this application that these claims, as originally presented, are not patentable over the references cited by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), as pertinent ones of the present claim amendments and cancellations are only for facilitating expeditious prosecution. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue the canceled claims and/or other claims in one or more continuing applications.
A telephonic interview regarding the instant matter was conducted on December 22,

2022, between Examiner Cindi Curry and Applicant's representatives, Steve Wang, 79,880 and Bianca Lindau (supervised by Steve Wang). Patentability under 35 U.S.C. § 103 was discussed. Applicant thanks the Examiner for their time and consideration in conducting the interview. No agreement was reached regarding proposed claim amendments. Applicant also addressed the fact that the Examiner did not address claims 18-20. They are as they stand.
The Office objected to the drawings, "as failing to comply with 37 CFR 1.84(p)(5)

because they do not include the following reference sign(s) mentioned in the description: fuel tank element 208." Office Action, p. 2. The Examiner is referring to para. [0023] of Applicant's specification, which states "As used herein, a "vent line" is a tether or a bundle of tethers, e.g., hose, tubing, cables, wires, and the like, which is configured to removably attach with a mating component of a vent of a fuel tank 208." "Fuel tank 208" is a clerical error and should read "fuel tank 108". Appropriate correction to the Specification has been made. Applicant respectfully submits that this rejection is now moot, and respectfully requests that this objection be withdrawn.
The Office further objected to the drawings under 37 CFR 1.83(a), for allegedly failing to show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. Id. Specifically, the Examiner stated

that the septum needed to be shown. FIG. 5 of the Drawings has been amended to include element 504, to indicate the (central) septum. Further, para. [0041] of the Specification has been amended to include element 504. Applicant respectfully submits that this rejection is now moot, and respectfully requests that this objection be withdrawn.

Claims 4-6 and 7 were rejected pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor regards as his invention.
Claim 4

The Office asserts that "[i]t is unclear which element is the septum." Office Action, p. 3. Without conceding the propriety of the rejection, and in the interest of advancing prosecution, Applicant respectfully submits that the amendment to FIG. 5 clarifies which element is "the septum" in claim 4. Further, the plural form of septum, "septa" is defined in para. [0015], which states, "However, in some embodiments, septa of multi-lobe tanks may be well-suited to support the structure of aircraft 112. As used herein, "septa" are partitions between objects, such as two fuel tanks. The plurality of fuel tanks may be divided by septa such that there is a septum between each fuel tank." Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 4 is clear. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that this rejection is now moot, and respectfully requests that this rejection of claim 4 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) be withdrawn. Claim 5

The Office asserts that "[i]t is unclear how the multi-lobe geometry provides tension." Office Action, p. 3. Applicant respectfully disagrees. Further, Applicant respectfully directs the Examiner's attention to paragraph [0050]. Para. [0050] states, "The multi-lobe geometry of the multi-lobe tanks 1300 may provide tension for each fuel tank 104 of the plurality of multi-lobe tanks tension may be achieved by equal pressure in each lobe of the geometry." Therefore, the Specification specifies how the multi-lobe geometry provides tension. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection.
The Office further asserts that "[i]t is unclear which element is the container." Id.
Without conceding the propriety of the rejection, and in the interest of advancing prosecution,

amendments presented in this paper have more distinctly claimed the subject matter regarded as the claimed invention in claim 5. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that this rejection is now moot, and respectfully requests that this rejection be withdrawn. Claim 6

The Office asserts that "[i]t is unclear in what the way the fuel tank is prepared. How the does the flight status affect this preparation?" Office Action, p. 4. Without conceding the propriety of the rejection, and in the interest of advancing prosecution, amendments presented in this paper have more distinctly claimed the subject matter regarded as the claimed invention in claim 6. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that this rejection is now moot, and respectfully requests that this rejection be withdrawn. Claim 17

The Office asserts that "[t]he term 'substantially' in claim 17 is a relative term which renders the claim indefinite. The term 'substantially' is not defined by the claim, the specification does not provide a standard for ascertaining the requisite degree, and one of ordinary skill in the art would not be reasonably apprised of the scope of the invention. Substantially is not a measurable term." Office Action, p. 4. Without conceding the propriety of the rejection, and in the interest of advancing prosecution, amendments presented in this paper have more distinctly claimed the subject matter regarded as the claimed invention in claim 17. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that this rejection is now moot, and respectfully requests that this rejection be withdrawn.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that all rejections of claims pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) be removed.
Rejection of claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103
Epstein/Glaser

Claims 1, 7-11, and 13-16 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over U.S. Patent App. No. 2015/0344143 to Epstein et al. (hereinafter "Epstein") and in view of U.S. Patent App. No. 2011/0042520 to Glaser et al. (hereinafter "Glaser"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claim 1
Claim 1 as amended recites

A method for SVG {EMBED HERE} 1.274.48 storing, using fueling, using
filling converts the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a signal that is then transmitted to a computing device; and removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft; and
preparing the fuel tank for flight as a function of the desired level; and flying, using the aircraft, a plurality of flights using the liquid gas fuel.

The Office Action takes official notice that it is allegedly well known to fill tanks to desired level and that the amount of fuel for more than one flight plus reserves and further relies on Glaser to allegedly teach, "removing the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft". Office Action, p. 5. Specifically, the Office Action refers to claim 7 of Glaser as allegedly teaching the second limitation. Id.
However, the Examiner has not taken official notice that nor suggested that Glaser

teaches, discloses, or suggests Applicant's claimed, "a sensor connected to the fuel tank detects at least abnormal phenomena related to the fuel tank, wherein the sensor converts the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a signal that is then transmitted to a computing device;" and "removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft." Applicant respectfully asserts that Glaser does not teach, suggest, or motivate Applicant's claimed, "a sensor connected to the fuel tank detects at least abnormal phenomena related to the fuel tank, wherein the sensor converts the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a signal that is then transmitted to a computing device;" and "removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Glaser fails to disclose, teach, or suggest, Applicant's particularly claimed limitations, as detailed above.
Epstein fails to cure the deficiencies of Glaser. The Office does not assert that Epstein
teaches, suggests, or motivates Applicant's claimed, "a sensor connected to the fuel tank detects

at least abnormal phenomena related to the fuel tank, wherein the sensor converts the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a signal that is then transmitted to a computing device;" and "removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft." Applicant respectfully asserts that Epstein does not teach, suggest, or motivate Applicant's claimed, "a sensor connected to the fuel tank detects at least abnormal phenomena related to the fuel tank, wherein the sensor converts the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a signal that is then transmitted to a computing device;" and "removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that none of what Epstein discloses, teaches, or suggests is Applicant's particularly claimed invention and claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser.

Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that Epstein and Glaser, alone or in any combination, fail to disclose, teach, or suggest, each claimed limitation, and the rejection to claim 1 has been overcome. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection.
Claims 7-11, and 13-16

Claims 7-11 and 13-16 depend, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that none of what Epstein and Glaser disclose, teach, or suggest is Applicant's particularly claimed invention and 7-11 and 13-16 are patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser, alone or in any combination.
